description: Code, frozen protocol, derived data and full results for a benchmark of probabilistic load forecasting in extreme cold: four PJM events (January 2014 polar vortex, February 2015 official-error anchor, December 2017 - January 2018 cold snap, December 2022 Winter Storm Elliott) and a replication on MISO (2017-18 cold snap, January 2019 polar vortex, Winter Storm Elliott) whose plan and criteria were fixed before any MISO data were inspected. Three forecaster families and five conformal calibrators are evaluated at a day-ahead (primary) and a one-hour horizon under strictly chronological evaluation and under retrospective leave-one-event-out transfer. Findings: uncalibrated 90% interval coverage collapses inside the events in both systems; no calibrator selected without the target event passes the repair test (0 of 6 cells in each system); retrospective and chronological coverage differ by double digits, overstating the temperature-stratified Mondrian calibrators in PJM (+11.6 and +21.2 pp) but with no consistent sign in MISO; replacing reanalysis temperature with archived GFS day-ahead forecasts for Elliott leaves uncalibrated event coverage unchanged. Version 1.1.0 adds the MISO replication (Amendment A4), the forecast-temperature arm (A3, post hoc) and the prior-winter calibration sensitivity (A2).
title: PJM and MISO Cold-Spell Calibration Benchmark: When Cold-Spell Calibration Fails to Transfer
